:::{#exr-double-complement-practice}
#### Taking the orthogonal complement twice

@thm-double-complement says that taking the [orthogonal complement](#def-orthogonal-complement)
of a [subspace](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace) twice gives back the subspace.
Let $\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 2)}$ in $\reals^2$,
whose orthogonal complement is $\mathcal{S}^\perp = \operatorname{span}\cb{(-2, 1)}$.

Find $(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$ directly from $\mathcal{S}^\perp = \operatorname{span}\cb{(-2, 1)}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

A vector $\vecf{w}$ is [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors) to every multiple of $(-2, 1)$
exactly when $-2 w_1 + w_2 = 0$.

:::
